evidence: Plaut. Cist. 4.2.17: āctumst; īlicet mē īnfēlīcem (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
Plaut. Trin. 3.4.194: āctum est dē collō meō (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
Traupman 105: it’s all over!, āctum est! or īlicet!
terms.comment: The perfect passive of agere, “it has been done”: nothing more can be done about it.
terms.grammar: impersonal perfect passive of agō; with dē + abl., it’s all up with

terms.gloss: it’s all over with (someone or something)
evidence: Plaut. Ps. 1.1.63: āctum hodiē est dē mē; Liv. 1.47 (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
terms.comment: “That’s the end of me” is āctum est dē mē.

terms.gloss: it’s all over! that’s the end!
evidence: Plaut. Cist. 4.2.17: āctumst; īlicet mē īnfēlīcem (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)
terms.comment: From īre licet, “you may go”, the formula that dismissed an assembly when its business was over (Lewis & Short); hence “it’s finished”. Not to be confused with īlicō, on the spot.

phrases.english: it’s all over; it’s finished, poor me
it’s all over with me today
by now it was all over with Servius

phrases.latin: Quid est? quid trepidās? … — Periimus: āctum est.
phrases.english: What is it? Why the panic? … — We’re done for: it’s all over.

sources: Lewis & Short: ago · Lewis & Short: ilicet
